subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What authorization and ownership rules should govern listing and terminating every managed exec run associated with a stored session?
rationale: The feature crosses session, process, node-host, and operator-scope boundaries; source evidence cannot determine whether arbitrary-session control should be admin-only, requester-owned, or deferred pending durable ownership.

options.title: Add admin-scoped controls
options.body: Introduce separate list and kill methods that require admin scope and operate only on supervisor records proven to match the canonical session owner.

options.title: Extend sessions.abort
options.body: Add an explicit terminate-children option to the write-scoped abort method with strict requester ownership checks and documented limitations.

options.title: Wait for durable ownership
options.body: Defer the public API until restart reconciliation can reliably identify and control previously tracked process trees.

recommendation.title: Add admin-scoped controls
recommendation.body: Introduce separate list and kill methods that require admin scope and operate only on supervisor records proven to match the canonical session owner.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects Vincent to session control, kill-route authorization, and the supervisor-facing surface.
